title: Observable Coding-Trace Early Warning
research_question: Given only an observable execution trace, can DSM issue an earlier reliable warning than conventional session signals?

current_source_assessment.reason: The source schema has no structured hypothesis set, confidence history, evidence relations, discriminating checks, action-pressure state, or fixed tool-call budget.

baseline_claim_boundary: These are ordinary deterministic trajectory summaries, not Coherence Dynamics metrics and not outcome predictions.

partitions.calibration: May select thresholds using calibration traces and calibration outcomes only.
partitions.freeze: The metric source, source schema, primary rule, thresholds, false-alarm target, and calibration hashes must be receiver-anchored before held-out outcomes are opened.
partitions.heldout_measurement: Receives source traces and the frozen profile only.
partitions.heldout_scoring: Opens hidden outcomes only after measurement hashes and the freeze are verified.

comparison.required_false_alarm_control: Compare warning time at the same held-out false-alarm rate.
comparison.success_condition: DSM must warn earlier than every declared conventional baseline without exceeding the matched false-alarm rate.
comparison.no_result_behavior: Report HOLD or UNDECIDABLE; do not tune a replacement metric on held-out failures.

paired_fixture.purpose: Prove that identical final aggregate statistics can conceal different event order.

claim_boundary: The bundled fixture validates strict normalization, free-text exclusion, trajectory preservation, and fail-closed metric availability. It does not establish predictive usefulness.
